sentences.en: For the last few months, I've been embedded in a number of right-wing and alt-right Discord servers.
sentences.zh: 过去几个月里，我潜伏在一些右翼和另类右翼的Discord服务器中。

sentences.en: I finagled access to their sort of inner sanctum chat rooms, so I could read what these guys are talking about when they think no one else is watching.
sentences.zh: 我设法进入了他们那种核心聊天室，这样我就能读到这些人在以为没别人看着时在讨论什么。

sentences.en: Let me ask you about Discord, because I went and Googled it, and it says, free voice and text chat for gamers.
sentences.zh: 让我问问你关于Discord的事，因为我特意去谷歌搜索了一下，上面说这是为游戏玩家提供的免费语音和文字聊天工具。

sentences.en: Yeah.

sentences.en: So Discord started as a chat app for people who play video games.
sentences.zh: Discord最初确实是为玩电子游戏的人设计的聊天应用。

sentences.en: It was like where you would go to talk with your Warcraft teammates and talk about strategy and stuff.
sentences.zh: 就像是你去和《魔兽世界》队友讨论战术之类的地方。

sentences.en: But several months ago, the alt-right and white nationalists discovered that, hey, this is a pretty secure platform.
sentences.zh: 但几个月前，另类右翼和白人民族主义者发现，嘿，这是一个相当安全的平台。

sentences.en: It allows us to be anonymous.
sentences.zh: 它允许我们保持匿名。

sentences.en: So this was a really good place for them to craft and sort of disseminate their message and organize their movement.
sentences.zh: 所以这对他们来说是一个非常好的地方，可以用来构建和传播他们的信息，并组织他们的运动。

sentences.en: Talk me through the first time that you got into one of these groups, these servers.
sentences.zh: 跟我讲讲你第一次进入这些群组、这些服务器时的情景。

sentences.en: Wow, that's really funny.
sentences.zh: 哇，那真的很有趣。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.zh: 有没有那种给新纳粹准备的约会网站？

sentences.zh: 比如，我想要一个。

sentences.en: A lot of it is people responding to the news.
sentences.zh: 很多内容是人们对新闻的反应。

sentences.en: They'll post in, you know, the latest thing that Trump tweeted or the latest story from the New York Times or CNN or somewhere else and talk about it.
sentences.zh: 他们会发布，你知道，特朗普最新发的推文，或者《纽约时报》、CNN或其他地方的最新报道，然后进行讨论。

sentences.en: You don't understand.
sentences.zh: 你不明白。

sentences.en: It's Trump's America.
sentences.zh: 这是特朗普的美国。

sentences.en: We can do whatever we want.
sentences.zh: 我们可以做任何我们想做的事。

sentences.en: And then sometimes they're doing sort of like movement building.
sentences.zh: 有时他们也在进行某种运动建设。

sentences.en: OK, the social justice movement we need to crush, not just sort of relegate to the background.
sentences.zh: 好的，我们需要粉碎社会正义运动，而不仅仅是将其边缘化。

sentences.en: We need to crush them, exterminate and annihilate them.
sentences.zh: 我们需要粉碎他们，消灭并彻底摧毁他们。

sentences.en: And we need to increase anti-Semitic feeling across the country.
sentences.zh: 我们需要在全国范围内加剧反犹太情绪。

sentences.en: And then everyone sort of responds with emojis.
sentences.zh: 然后每个人都会用表情包来回应。

sentences.en: So emojis are big.
sentences.zh: 所以表情包很重要。

sentences.en: Tell me about the emojis.
sentences.zh: 跟我说说这些表情包。

sentences.zh: 表情包是其中的重要组成部分，因为你实际上可以在

sentences.zh: 你知道，他说你可以选择蓝色药丸或红色药丸。

sentences.en: Wow.

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: No.
sentences.zh: 不。

sentences.zh: 所以他们经常使用这个词。

sentences.en: Feels like a very young, what you're describing, kind of millennial way of interacting.
sentences.zh: 你描述的这种互动方式感觉非常年轻，很像千禧一代的风格。

sentences.en: This is just the beginning.
sentences.zh: 这仅仅是个开始。

sentences.en: Something that I really want to push for, a removal of hate speech policies on like YouTube so we can start posting our content there again.
sentences.zh: 我真正想推动的一件事，是取消YouTube等平台上的仇恨言论政策，这样我们就能重新开始在那里发布我们的内容。

sentences.en: Then we can start like red pilling the normies.
sentences.zh: 然后我们就可以开始给普通人“喂红药丸”了。

sentences.zh: 但为了能够发帖，你必须提交一张展示你白皮肤的照片。

sentences.zh: 这是明确要求的吗？

sentences.en: Yeah.

sentences.en: Let me see if I can find the screenshot.
sentences.zh: 让我看看能不能找到那张截图。

sentences.en: Yeah, here we go.
sentences.zh: 对，就是这个。

sentences.en: So it says, here are the membership requirements for the Alt-Right channel.
sentences.zh: 上面写着，这是“另类右翼”频道的会员要求。

sentences.en: Submit a photo to a staff member of your arm, hand, leg, or face to prove that you are indeed white, along with your username
sentences.zh: 向工作人员提交一张你的手臂、手、腿或脸的照片，以证明你确实是白人，同时照片里要写上你的用户名

sentences.en: written down somewhere in the photo to prove that it is indeed a picture of you.
sentences.zh: 以证明这确实是你本人的照片。

sentences.en: You took a photograph of yourself.
sentences.zh: 你拍了你自己的照片？

sentences.en: I did not.
sentences.zh: 我没有。

sentences.en: I never applied for formal membership.
sentences.zh: 我从未申请正式会员资格。

sentences.en: So I was just a lurker.
sentences.zh: 所以我只是个潜水员。

sentences.en: I could read what was going on in the big channels.
sentences.zh: 我可以阅读大频道里发生的事情。

sentences.en: So did you notice any notable divisions within the group?
sentences.zh: 那你有没有注意到群组内部有什么明显的派系分歧？

sentences.en: I mean, people who were uncomfortable with the overtness of the racism, people who were kind of debating what their presentation ought to be.
sentences.zh: 我是说，有些人对这种露骨的种族主义感到不适，有些人则在争论他们的立场应该是什么样的。

sentences.en: What did that look like?
sentences.zh: 那是什么样子的？

sentences.en: Yeah, I mean, that was one of the most interesting things that I saw was sort of these internal debates.
sentences.zh: 是的，我的意思是，我看到的最有趣的事情之一就是这些内部辩论。

sentences.en: I thought we had this conversation yesterday.
sentences.zh: 我以为我们昨天已经谈过这个了。

sentences.en: I literally asked you guys, what percentage of white would you consider white?
sentences.zh: 我真的问过你们，你们认为多少比例的白人血统才算白人？

sentences.en: And you said 87.5.
And guess what?

sentences.en: I'm 87.5% white.

sentences.en: Yo, hey guys, Europeans, let's move to another channel where there's no...
sentences.zh: 嘿，伙计们，欧洲人，让我们换个频道，那里没有……

sentences.en: Where you have people saying, you know, what's our slate of beliefs?
sentences.zh: 你会看到有人在说，你知道，我们的信仰纲领是什么？

sentences.en: What's our platform?
sentences.zh: 我们的平台是什么？

sentences.en: My views on Christianity being revised, if you just look at...
sentences.zh: 我对基督教的看法正在修正，如果你看看……

sentences.en: He just, he wanted to talk about Christianity and he wants Christianity to be revived to save the WeSt.
sentences.zh: 他只是想谈论基督教，他希望复兴基督教以拯救西方。

sentences.en: You know, there were divides among, do we let women into our movement?
sentences.zh: 你知道，他们之间存在分歧，比如我们是否让女性加入我们的运动？

sentences.en: Are we anti-Semitic or are we more pro-white?
sentences.zh: 我们是反犹太主义者，还是更倾向于支持白人？

sentences.en: There were divides about whether or not posting swastikas hurt the movement or not, because to the outside world, it would just look like, oh, these guys are Nazis.
sentences.zh: 关于发布纳粹万字旗是否会损害运动，他们也有分歧，因为在外界看来，这看起来就像是，哦，这些人是纳粹。

sentences.en: And they wanted to sort of carve out their own identity as like a new kind of white nationalist movement.
sentences.zh: 他们想把自己塑造成一种新型白人民族主义运动的身份。

sentences.en: Kevin, when does Charlottesville first come up within this online group?
sentences.zh: 凯文，夏洛茨维尔事件是什么时候在这个在线群组中首次被提及的？

sentences.en: I started seeing references to Charlottesville maybe a month before the rally itself.
sentences.zh: 我在集会前大约一个月就开始看到关于夏洛茨维尔的提及了。

sentences.en: This rally is for, the purpose of this is to gain sympathy for pro-white advocacy, as well as a general uniting of the right wing.
sentences.zh: 这次集会的目的是为了争取对白人权益倡导的支持，以及实现右翼的全面联合。

sentences.en: There were a lot of people arranging carpools and talking about, you know, where to find lodging and...
sentences.zh: 有很多人在安排拼车，讨论，你知道，去哪里找住宿，以及……

sentences.en: More of the details, but anyone who doesn't have tiki torches now should go out and get it basically tonight or tomorrow morning.
sentences.zh: 更多细节，但基本上现在没有火把的人今晚或明早应该去买一个。

sentences.en: What to wear was a big thing.
sentences.zh: 穿什么也是一件大事。

sentences.en: Some of the sort of younger white nationalists were sort of rolling their eyes at some of the groups like the KKK and the sort of more millennial neo-Nazis
sentences.zh: 一些比较年轻的白人民族主义者对三K党之类的组织翻白眼，而那些千禧一代的新纳粹分子

sentences.en: would say like, oh God, those guys are so embarrassing.
sentences.zh: 会说，天哪，那些人太尴尬了。

sentences.en: Like, they're these boomers with their hoods and their robes and they're just like so cringeworthy.
sentences.zh: 就像，那些戴着头套和长袍的婴儿潮一代，他们真是太让人尴尬了。

sentences.en: That's fascinating.
sentences.zh: 这太令人着迷了。

sentences.en: Essentially, do not be wearing face coverings or masks.
sentences.zh: 本质上，不要戴面罩或口罩。

sentences.en: It's like an old KKK thing.
sentences.zh: 那像是老三K党那一套。

sentences.en: So they were sort of advocating for just a more normal business casual clothes or wear polo shirts and khakis and make themselves look sort of more presentable.
sentences.zh: 所以他们主张穿更普通的商务休闲装，或者穿Polo衫和卡其裤，让自己看起来更体面一些。

sentences.en: I mean, these are not people who want to emulate the fringe status of older groups of white nationalists.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这些人并不想效仿老一代白人民族主义者那种边缘化的状态。

sentences.en: They really want to sort of take this to the mainstream.
sentences.zh: 他们真的想把这一套推向主流。

sentences.en: And I guess appearance looking like the kid next door or the guy in the next cubicle is something that they're conscious of.
sentences.zh: 我想，看起来像邻家男孩或隔壁工位同事那样的外表，是他们非常在意的事情。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And if you look at the footage of Charlottesville, like it's a jumble.
sentences.zh: 如果你看夏洛茨维尔的录像，那简直是一团糟。

sentences.en: I mean, there are swastika tattoos and military helmets.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，有万字旗纹身和军用头盔。

sentences.en: And then there are guys who look like maybe they just got lost on the way to the insurance convention.
sentences.zh: 然后还有些人看起来像是去参加保险会议迷路了。

sentences.en: If you don't have a torch, go to the front of the line.
sentences.zh: 如果你没有火把，就去队伍前面。

sentences.en: And then we actually get to Charlottesville and suddenly this online thing has a physical manifestation.
sentences.zh: 然后我们真的到了夏洛茨维尔，突然间，这个在线上的东西有了物理表现。

sentences.en: I wonder what that was like to see it all come together back online in the chat rooMs. Well, so some of it was happening in real time.
sentences.zh: 我很好奇在聊天室里看到这一切汇聚在一起是什么感觉。嗯，所以其中一些是在实时发生的。

sentences.en: I mean, they were giving updates to each other.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，他们当时在互相通报最新情况。

sentences.en: It was probably around, we're definitely above 600 at this point.
sentences.zh: 当时人数大概在……我们现在肯定已经超过600人了。

sentences.en: I can't even see the end of the line.
sentences.zh: 我甚至看不到队伍的尽头。

sentences.en: It just keeps going.
sentences.zh: 它还在不断延伸。

sentences.en: And then there was just like a lot of sideline cheerleading.
sentences.zh: 然后场边还有很多加油助威的人。

sentences.en: So the people who weren't there, who were just observing on Discord, you know, were posting, hail our people, hail victory.
sentences.zh: 所以那些没去现场、只是在Discord上围观的人，你知道，都在发帖说，向我们的人致敬，向胜利致敬。

sentences.en: Hail victory!
sentences.zh: 向胜利致敬！

sentences.en: But when it turned violent, that's when you saw people making what, you know, to my mind were some of the most offensive statements that I've ever seen on Discord.
sentences.zh: 但当事态演变成暴力冲突时，你就会看到人们发表了一些在我看来是Discord上出现过的最令人反感的言论。

sentences.en: Making fun of Heather Heyer, the woman who was killed.
sentences.zh: 嘲笑希瑟·海耶，那位遇害的女性。

sentences.en: One well-known white nationalist started to try to organize to go to her funeral and make a show of force.
sentences.zh: 一位知名的白人民族主义者开始组织人手去参加她的葬礼，并进行武力示威。

sentences.en: I mean, really just the lowest of the low.
sentences.zh: 我是说，这真的是卑劣到了极点。

sentences.en: And I think that's when Discord actually started to take notice too.
sentences.zh: 我想也就是从那时起，Discord才真正开始注意到这个问题。

sentences.en: So tell me what actually happened after Charlottesville to this online group that had been hosted on Discord.
sentences.zh: 那么告诉我，夏洛茨维尔事件之后，这个在Discord上托管的在线群体到底发生了什么？

sentences.en: So on Monday after the rally, Discord banned the alt-right server and a number of other prominent right-wing and white nationalist servers.
sentences.zh: 集会后的周一，Discord封禁了那个另类右翼服务器，以及其他一些知名的右翼和白人民族主义服务器。

sentences.en: Was that a surprise for you?
sentences.zh: 这对你来说是个意外吗？

sentences.en: You cover these companies and think about them a lot.
sentences.zh: 你一直在报道这些公司，对它们思考良多。

sentences.en: I mean,
sentences.zh: 我是说，

sentences.en: I had been reporting on this for weeks and asking them, so what are you going to do about these white nationalists?
sentences.zh: 我对此已经报道了几个星期，一直在问他们，你们打算怎么处理这些白人民族主义者？

sentences.en: What, you know, what's your game plan?
sentences.zh: 你们的应对计划是什么？

sentences.en: And they had sort of been taking a hands-off approach.
sentences.zh: 他们一直采取的是一种不干涉的态度。

sentences.en: I mean, they said they're responsible for policing themselves.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，他们说他们有责任进行自我监管。

sentences.en: My hunch was that they would have to address this eventually.
sentences.zh: 我的直觉是，他们最终不得不解决这个问题。

sentences.en: I hoped that it wouldn't come to an event like this.
sentences.zh: 我希望事情不会发展到这种地步。

sentences.en: Do you, do you think that Charlottesville happens because people are able to organize online in a forum like this?
sentences.zh: 你认为夏洛茨维尔事件的发生，是因为人们能够像这样在在线论坛上组织起来吗？

sentences.en: Yes, I do.
sentences.zh: 是的，我认为是。

sentences.en: It's kind of fascinating and a little counter-historical to imagine that if with a single click of a button, a company like Discord could have deleted this forum.
sentences.zh: 想象一下，如果Discord这样的公司只需点击一个按钮就能删除这个论坛，这既令人着迷，又有点违背历史。

sentences.en: Well, that raises a lot of complicated questions about free speech and everything else, but that they could have.
sentences.zh: 嗯，这引发了许多关于言论自由及其他方面的复杂问题，但他们确实有能力这样做。

sentences.en: I think it's a real question that I think they're going to have to contend with.
sentences.zh: 我认为这是一个他们必须面对的现实问题。

sentences.en: Could we have done something sooner?
sentences.zh: 我们本可以早点采取行动吗？

sentences.en: I mean, the reality is that there are white nationalists before Discord.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，现实情况是，在Discord出现之前就有白人民族主义者了。

sentences.en: There will be white nationalists after Discord.
sentences.zh: 在Discord之后也依然会有白人民族主义者。

sentences.en: But I think one of the lessons of the past couple of weeks is that these movements actually do depend on having stable,
sentences.zh: 但我认为过去几周的教训之一是，这些运动确实依赖于拥有稳定、

sentences.en: good technology infrastructure.
sentences.zh: 良好的技术基础设施。

sentences.en: It's much easier to organize if you have a central gathering place.
sentences.zh: 如果你有一个中心聚集地，组织起来就容易多了。

sentences.en: People know where to find you.
sentences.zh: 人们知道去哪里找到你。

sentences.en: People know where to find you.
sentences.zh: 人们知道去哪里找到你。

sentences.en: But I think what we've seen in recent weeks is that a number of tech companies are getting very uncomfortable with their role in these extremist movements.
sentences.zh: 但我认为我们最近几周看到的是，许多科技公司对它们在这些极端主义运动中所扮演的角色感到非常不安。

sentences.en: I mean, we've seen Google and PayPal and GoDaddy take actions to kick these guys off their services.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我们已经看到谷歌、PayPal和GoDaddy采取行动，将这些人踢出了他们的服务平台。

sentences.en: So what will they do next?
sentences.zh: 那么他们接下来会做什么？

sentences.en: These people find a way.
sentences.zh: 这些人总能找到办法。

sentences.en: When they're kicked off one platform, they find somewhere else to organize.
sentences.zh: 当他们被一个平台踢出后，他们会找到其他地方继续组织活动。

sentences.en: And so if they are kicked off of these big, you know, well-functioning tech platforms, they're either going to have to find worse alternatives or they're
sentences.zh: 所以，如果他们被这些大型、运作良好的科技平台踢出，他们要么必须寻找更糟糕的替代品，要么

sentences.en: going to have to build their own.
sentences.zh: 就必须建立自己的平台。

sentences.en: And that's an expensive and hard process.
sentences.zh: 那是一个昂贵且艰难的过程。

sentences.en: So at some point, you actually spoke with one of the organizers of this online group and of the rally in Charlottesville.
sentences.zh: 所以，你曾经和这个在线群体以及夏洛茨维尔集会的组织者之一谈过话。

sentences.en: Tell me about your interactions with him.
sentences.zh: 跟我说说你与他的互动吧。

sentences.en: I mean, I would say it was it was bizarre.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我会说这很离奇。

sentences.en: Hey, Kevin, how you doing?
sentences.zh: 嘿，凯文，你好吗？

sentences.en: What's going on?
sentences.zh: 怎么了？

sentences.en: This is a guy named Nathan Gate.
sentences.zh: 这是一个叫内森·盖特的人。

sentences.en: He goes by the username TheBigKK.
sentences.zh: 他的用户名是TheBigKK。

sentences.en: Thanks for getting back to me.
sentences.zh: 谢谢你回复我。

sentences.en: I appreciate it.
sentences.zh: 我很感激。

sentences.en: No problem.
sentences.zh: 没问题。

sentences.en: And he is a very prominent force behind getting together some of the people at Charlottesville.
sentences.zh: 他是促成夏洛茨维尔集会人员聚集背后的一个非常突出的力量。

sentences.en: Why you guys gravitate toward Discord as opposed to other platforMs.
sentences.zh: 为什么你们这些人比起其他平台更倾向于使用Discord？

sentences.en: So we had a normal interview about his relationship to Discord.
sentences.zh: 所以我们进行了一次关于他与Discord关系的正常采访。

sentences.en: And the reason people aren't moving to Discord is quite simply because Discord's a lot better in every possible way.
sentences.zh: 人们之所以转向Discord，原因很简单，因为Discord在各方面都好得多。

sentences.en: I've reported on a lot of alt-right members and white supremacists.
sentences.zh: 我报道过很多另类右翼成员和白人至上主义者。

sentences.en: And there always is a moment where it sort of crosses the line to something more personal.
sentences.zh: 总会有那么一个时刻，事情会越界变得更加个人化。

sentences.en: Do you mind if I ask you a question?
sentences.zh: 你介意我问你一个问题吗？

sentences.en: He sort of stopped and said, well, can I ask you a question?
sentences.zh: 他停顿了一下说，好吧，我能问你一个问题吗？

sentences.en: Yeah, go for it.
sentences.zh: 可以，问吧。

sentences.en: It's a bit personal.
sentences.zh: 这有点私人。

sentences.en: What race are you?
sentences.zh: 你是哪个种族的？

sentences.en: You've seen my profile picture.
sentences.zh: 你见过我的头像了。

sentences.en: Yes, you look Hispanic to me.
sentences.zh: 是的，在我看来你像西班牙裔。

sentences.en: I'm not Hispanic.
sentences.zh: 我不是西班牙裔。

sentences.en: Are you white or are you Jewish is the question.
sentences.zh: 问题是，你是白人还是犹太人？

sentences.en: Well, if you're white, then see you in a few years.
sentences.zh: 好吧，如果你是白人，那几年后再见。

sentences.en: You'll be part of this group in a few years.
sentences.zh: 几年后你就会成为这个群体的一员了。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: All right.
sentences.zh: 好吧。

sentences.en: Have a good day.
sentences.zh: 祝你今天愉快。

sentences.en: And it requires a certain detachment, too.
sentences.zh: 这也需要一定的超然态度。

sentences.en: Because I actually did want to interview these guys and know what it was like.
sentences.zh: 因为我确实想采访这些人，了解他们的想法。

sentences.en: And obviously, I don't want to be a mouthpiece for their views, which I find abhorrent.
sentences.zh: 显然，我不想成为他们观点的传声筒，我觉得那些观点令人厌恶。

sentences.en: But I also feel like it can be useful to talk to these people because they are on the front lines of a movement that I think we all have realized we can't ignore.
sentences.zh: 但我也觉得与这些人交谈是有用的，因为他们处于一场我们都意识到无法忽视的运动的最前线。

sentences.en: Kevin, thank you very much.
sentences.zh: 凯文，非常感谢你。

sentences.en: Thank you for having me.
sentences.zh: 谢谢你邀请我。

sentences.en: Next week, we'll talk to a man who grew up in one of the most prominent white nationalist families in the United States and then left.
sentences.zh: 下周，我们将采访一位在美国最著名的白人民族主义家庭中长大，后来又离开的人。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: Hey, I'm Benjamin Poulin.
sentences.zh: 嘿，我是本杰明·普兰。

sentences.en: And I'm Mark Ronson.
sentences.zh: 我是马克·朗森。

sentences.en: And welcome to The Reframers, a podcast that's all about the love of design and the culture that surrounds it.
sentences.zh: 欢迎收听《重构者》，这是一个关于设计之爱及其周边文化的播客。

sentences.en: Even back when I was DJing in nightclubs in the era of vinyl, every night, you took 300 of your most prized possessions to work with you.
sentences.zh: 即使在我还在黑胶唱片时代去夜店当DJ的时候，每天晚上，你都要带着300件你最珍贵的宝贝去上班。

sentences.en: And you turned a DJ booth into this like living pop-up museum of beautiful 50-year-old artifacts.
sentences.zh: 你把DJ台变成了一个充满活力的快闪博物馆，里面陈列着美丽的50年历史的艺术品。

sentences.en: Listen to The Reframers from Audemars Piguet now on your favorite podcast platforMs.
sentences.zh: 现在就在你最喜欢的播客平台上收听爱彼出品的《重构者》吧。

sentences.en: The New York Times app?
sentences.zh: 《纽约时报》应用程序？

sentences.en: Unlocked?
sentences.zh: 解锁版？

sentences.en: Everyone knows you need to subscribe to The Times to access all of the reporting.
sentences.zh: 大家都知道你需要订阅《时报》才能阅读所有报道。

sentences.en: But what if you could explore The Times for a month, for free, without putting in a credit card?
sentences.zh: 但如果你能免费试用《时报》一个月，而且无需输入信用卡信息呢？

sentences.en: Now you can.
sentences.zh: 现在你可以了。

sentences.en: When you download The New York Times app for the first time, your first month in the app is free.
sentences.zh: 当你第一次下载《纽约时报》应用程序时，你在应用里的第一个月是免费的。

sentences.en: A month to go behind the paywall to see what Times subscribers get every single day.
sentences.zh: 用一个月的时间突破付费墙，看看《时报》订阅者每天都能获得什么。

sentences.en: If you don't already subscribe to The New York Times, download The Times app today and get free access for 30 days.
sentences.zh: 如果你还没有订阅《纽约时报》，今天就下载《时报》应用程序，获得30天的免费访问权限。

sentences.en: Here's what else you need to know today.
sentences.zh: 以下是你今天还需要知道的其他消息。

sentences.en: The Islamic State is claiming credit for a deadly terrorist attack in Barcelona on Thursday that has left at least 13 people dead and at least 80 injured, and yet another instance
sentences.zh: 伊斯兰国声称对周四发生在巴塞罗那的致命恐怖袭击负责，袭击造成至少13人死亡，至少80人受伤，这是又一起

sentences.en: of extremists using vehicles as weapons in European cities.
sentences.zh: 极端分子在欧洲城市使用车辆作为武器的案例。

sentences.en: The Times reports that just before 6 p.m., a white van started plowing through the city's
sentences.zh: 《时报》报道称，下午6点前不久，一辆白色货车开始冲进该市

sentences.en: most famous street, weaving back and forth, apparently trying to hit as many people as possible.
sentences.zh: 最著名的街道，来回穿梭，显然是想尽可能多地撞人。

sentences.en: Early Friday, Spanish police reported killing four people in a seaside town 70 miles south of Barcelona in an attempt to stop what might have been a second-plan attack.
sentences.zh: 周五早些时候，西班牙警方报告称，在巴塞罗那以南70英里的一个海滨小镇击毙了四人，试图阻止可能发生的第二次袭击计划。

sentences.en: And two women in the middle of the violence in Charlottesville last Saturday have sued more than two dozen leaders, groups, and websites aligned with the alt-right.
sentences.zh: 上周六在夏洛茨维尔暴力事件中的两名女性起诉了二十多个与另类右翼结盟的领导人、团体和网站。

sentences.en: Taydrent and Micah Washington weren't part of the proteSt.
sentences.zh: 泰德伦特和米卡·华盛顿并不是抗议活动的一部分。

sentences.en: As they told The Times, they were just on their way home when they got stuck in traffic.
sentences.zh: 正如她们告诉《时报》的那样，她们只是在回家路上被堵在了车流中。

sentences.en: I was driving.
sentences.zh: 当时我在开车。

sentences.en: I made a right at the stop sign.
sentences.zh: 我在停车标志处右转。

sentences.en: The rally people were right there.
sentences.zh: 集会的人就在那里。

sentences.en: I got to the stoplight, and they had all the roads blocked off.
sentences.zh: 我开到红绿灯处，他们把所有的路都封死了。

sentences.en: It was like a one-way, so you couldn't go nowhere.
sentences.zh: 那是一条单行道，所以你哪儿也去不了。

sentences.en: It was like we was just stuck because all the people was coming towards us, trying to go back to the downtown mall.
sentences.zh: 我们就像被困住了，因为所有人都朝我们涌来，试图回到市中心的购物中心。

sentences.en: They were surrounding my car.
sentences.zh: 他们包围了我的车。

sentences.en: We didn't feel like we were in any type of danger.
sentences.zh: 我们当时并不觉得有任何危险。

sentences.en: Yeah, they weren't doing nothing.
sentences.zh: 是的，他们什么也没做。

sentences.en: We weren't scared.
sentences.zh: 我们并不害怕。

sentences.en: I actually remember the last thing this guy looked at me, and he said, thank you for your patience.
sentences.zh: 我其实记得最后那个人看着我，他说，谢谢你的耐心。

sentences.en: Next thing I know, out of nowhere, I just hear a big boom in my head just going into the stairwell.
sentences.zh: 接下来我只知道，不知从哪儿传来一声巨响，我的头就撞向了楼梯间。

sentences.en: As soon as my head went to the stairwell, I tried to get myself back up, and I see this
sentences.zh: 当我的头撞向楼梯间时，我试图爬起来，然后我看到这个

sentences.en: woman basically laying on my window, you know, and I'm trying to grasp, like, am I seeing what I'm seeing?
sentences.zh: 女人基本上趴在我的车窗上，你知道，我试图理解，我看到的是真的吗？

sentences.en: So I think I kind of went into a shock.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为我有点休克了。

sentences.en: I closed my eyes.
sentences.zh: 我闭上了眼睛。

sentences.en: I think my sister said I was shaking.
sentences.zh: 我想我姐姐说我在发抖。

sentences.en: I don't recall that.
sentences.zh: 我不记得了。

sentences.en: I just remember closing my eyes, and I just remember just panicking, I guess.
sentences.zh: 我只记得我闭上了眼睛，我只记得我当时陷入了恐慌。

sentences.en: What I saw before I got hit was a beautiful thing.
sentences.zh: 我在被撞之前看到的是一件美好的事情。

sentences.en: I didn't see racism.
sentences.zh: 我没有看到种族主义。

sentences.en: The crowd that I observed was standing up for something.
sentences.zh: 我观察到的人群是在为某种东西挺身而出。

sentences.en: It was actually, it was amazing to watch, you know, so many people shouting Black Lives
sentences.zh: 看着那么多人高喊“黑人的命也是命”，这真的很

sentences.en: Matter.
sentences.zh: 了不起。

sentences.en: It was amazing to watch so many white people more than black people who were doing that.
sentences.zh: 看着那么多白人，比黑人还多，在做这件事，真是太令人惊叹了。

sentences.en: You know, I never saw that before, to be honest with you.
sentences.zh: 老实说，我以前从未见过这种情况。

sentences.en: I feel like that, that right there, to know that they was just peacefully staying up for something, and all hell broke loose in five seconds, something's wrong with that.
sentences.zh: 我觉得，就那一点，知道他们只是在和平地为某件事挺身而出，结果五秒钟内就乱成了一团，这肯定有什么不对劲。

sentences.en: That affect me.
sentences.zh: 这影响了我。

sentences.en: That affect me to know you can't be walking down the street, peacefully minding your business,
sentences.zh: 这让我意识到，你不能和平地走在街上处理自己的事情，

sentences.en: and just because you got somebody's hatred in their heart, your life can be gone that faSt.
sentences.zh: 仅仅因为有人心中怀有仇恨，你的生命就会如此迅速地消逝。

sentences.en: You know, something is wrong with this.
sentences.zh: 你知道，这肯定有什么不对劲。

sentences.zh: 本周的《Wirecutter秀》，我们正在为假期接待客人做准备。

sentences.zh: 敬请收听关于如何让客人感到宾至如归的建议。

sentences.en: Are they a blackout sleeper?
sentences.zh: 他们是那种一沾枕头就睡着的人吗？

sentences.en: I don't mean do they blackout to go to sleep.
sentences.zh: 我不是指他们喝断片了才去睡觉。

sentences.en: I mean, what kind of light do they require?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，它们需要什么样的光照？

sentences.en: Because that is a very specific thing.
sentences.zh: 因为那是非常具体的要求。

sentences.en: Do they have allergies, food sensitivities?
sentences.zh: 它们有过敏症或食物敏感吗？

sentences.en: Are they coffee tea drinkers?
sentences.zh: 它们是喝咖啡还是喝茶？

sentences.en: What time do they like to get up?
sentences.zh: 它们喜欢几点起床？

sentences.en: Find The Wirecutter Show on the New York Times app or wherever you like to listen.
sentences.zh: 请在《纽约时报》应用程序或你喜欢的任何平台上收听《The Wirecutter Show》。
